items.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023
items.q: applying the things that he got from Larry Young

ctx.x: See Woody’s the perfect example of that. Because Woody’s music was harmonically very intellectual. He included rhythmic elements from Brazil and as well as Afro- Caribbean rhythms and swing. And when he soloed he was applying harmonic concepts that were not really that closely related to trumpet. They’re mostly related to saxophone performance. But he played lyrically and beautiful even when he was playing his most abstract lines it was always beautiful. “Sweet Love of Mine” — beautiful composition. Woody could…

What is it — you know Phil Woods said that he didn’t consider himself an innovator, he was a craftsman. And maybe — I don’t know how you look at your own playing but does it get harder as time goes by to become an innovator? To come up with something that’s new?
